title: Intrinsic-Dimension-Guided Bottleneck Selection for Autoencoders and Variational Autoencoders with Active-Unit Diagnostics
content: The bottleneck dimension m of autoencoders (AEs) and variational autoencoders (VAEs) is usually set by convention or trial and error. We propose a conditional, diagnostic protocol that uses an intrinsic-dimension estimate d^ID of the input data as a search-window reference for m: AEs are searched within m∈[d^ID,2d^ID], whereas VAEs receive a generous candidate m≥2d^ID whose surplus coordinates are verified after training using active units (AU) and reconstruction error. The protocol is motivated by a topological lower bound for zero-error continuous reconstruction and by a linear-Gaussian rate–distortion surrogate with activation condition λj>βτ2. Under the tested settings, the protocol produced reproducible diagnostics on synthetic manifolds (three to five seeds) and on fully connected VAEs for MNIST and Fashion-MNIST (three seeds each): MNIST passes, Fashion-MNIST is diagnosed as an over-pruning boundary case, and for the specific MNIST grid and evaluation protocol used here the ID-guided window reduces training runs by roughly 60–80% while containing the best observed linear-probe accuracy. The method is conditional: intrinsic-dimension estimates were stable only through reference representations with m≫d^ID, latent-space TwoNN estimates on natural images increased beyond a provisional consistency region, and the tested Conv-VAE schedule (βmax=4) showed no truncation, with larger βmax reducing the activation ratio without order consistency. We therefore position d^ID as a search-window reference and AU as a model- and training-dependent diagnostic—not as general estimators of intrinsic or embedding dimension.
